actions: Name a security owner and define responsibilities (a simple RACI is enough).
Create a basic risk register and review the top risks monthly.
Approve and publish core security policies (acceptable use, access control, incident response).
Enable MFA for email, admin accounts, and remote access first.
Set a monthly patch cycle and track completion for critical systems.
Harden endpoints: disk encryption, EDR/AV, and secure configuration baselines.
Document and test an incident response plan (who to call, what to do, when).
Turn on key logs (email/admin, endpoints, firewall) and review alerts weekly.
Run regular vulnerability scans and track remediation.
Create a simple asset inventory (devices, cloud accounts, key services).
Classify data into 3 labels (Public/Internal/Confidential) and apply them.
Review backups: retention, offsite copy, and perform a restore test.
List your critical suppliers and what data/systems they access.
Add security clauses to new contracts (breech notification, minimum controls).
Run lightweight due diligence for critical suppliers annually.
Deliver short awareness training and include it in onboarding.
Create an easy way to report suspicious emails or incidents.
Share one monthly security tip and make it normal to ask questions.
Implement joiner/mover/leaver checklists and approvals for access.
Review privileged access quarterly and remove what is not needed.
Use phishing-resistant controls where possible (MFA + training).
Define business continuity basics: top critical services and recovery steps.
Test backups and recovery for at least one critical system each quarter.
Set simple RTO/RPO targets and track improvements.
